title: ENTITY v3.4.0 Documentation Portal
text: Operator, developer, protocol, economic, security and generated reference documentation for ENTITY Global Passport & Continuous Provenance. Current protected release: v3.4.0 , release commit 2db5bff64507b8d67642122a5ff2fc73dfef9152 . This portal is documentation, not an authority root. Exact code, signed records, manifests, schemas and qualification evidence control their respective claims. Operators: install, run, ingest, verify, back up, recover and troubleshoot. Developers: architecture, APIs, SDK/CLI, profiles, schemas, packages, tests and interoperability. Protocol reviewers: sovereignty, evidence, rights, portability and market lifecycle. Economic reviewers: rights instruments, participation, settlement and value boundaries.

title: Operator Manual
text: Operate ENTITY v3.4.0 without collapsing custody into authority. Protect keys and state, verify content and passports, and preserve provider independence.

title: Install v3.4.0
text: Pin deployments to the immutable v3.4.0 tag or an explicitly approved later commit. Use a dedicated Python environment and keep production identity keys outside the repository.

title: Production State Layout
text: Separate reviewed code from runtime state. A practical deployment has core/, state/, exports/ and logs/. The state/identity tree is sovereign material and must never be committed.

title: Identity and Key Operations
text: ENTITY identities are cryptographic roots, not usernames. Human-readable aliases resolve to an ent2 identity but do not replace it. Protect signing and recovery keys and never expose private bytes in logs.

title: Aliases and Sovereign Domains
text: Aliases and .entity names are resolution surfaces. Binding hashes and cryptographic roots prevent a readable name from silently becoming sovereign authority.

title: Install Global Profiles
text: The Global profile is required. Industry profiles compose on top of it and fail closed when parents or constraints are missing. Profiles constrain interpretation; they do not create authority.

title: Ingest a File
text: Continuous ingestion hashes content, registers an object, creates evidence and rights, issues Rights and Global Passports, stores content-addressed custody and records POTENTIAL/0 economic state.

title: Ingest a Directory
text: Bound recursive ingestion to a known corpus. Exclude .git, dependency trees, virtual environments, caches and generated build output unless those artifacts are intentionally in scope.

title: Evidence Operations
text: Evidence Objects bind source Entity, evidence type, subject, content hash and provenance. Signatures prove attribution/integrity within scope; they do not make an external-world assertion objectively true.

title: Rights Passport Operations
text: Rights Passports bind objects to explicit rights rules, custody, provenance, privacy and bounded economic terms. Access and custody are not ownership.

title: Global Passport Operations
text: A Global Passport binds one object to its Rights Passport, profile stack, evidence, provenance, mappings and economic state. Verify controller alignment and all referenced records.

title: Verify a Passport
text: Verification establishes protocol integrity for supplied state, not objective truth or regulatory compliance. Use the v3.4 CLI or SDK against the state containing the referenced registries.

title: Backup and Recovery
text: Back up identity, registries, content-addressed custody and databases needed to reconstruct authoritative state. Recovery must preserve the same Entity root and semantic result.

title: Sovereign Export and Portability
text: Export enough governed state to verify identity, authority, rights, evidence, provenance and content commitments without requiring BTG hosting or a specific provider.

title: Security Operations
text: Treat authorization failures, signature failures, rollback anomalies and content-hash mismatches as security events. Never commit keys, credentials or live state databases.

title: Upgrade and Version Control
text: Pin the source version, verify release evidence, back up state, test migration and preserve the old verification path. Historical signed semantics are never silently reinterpreted.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Common failures include missing cryptography dependencies, missing Global profile, controller/passport mismatch, bad content hashes and permission errors. Fix the cause rather than bypassing guards.

title: Production Checklist
text: Before service: pin release; verify tests/hashes; load intended identities; verify signing/recovery; install profiles; confirm backup paths; run controlled ingest; verify the resulting passport; record deployment evidence.

title: Incident Response
text: Contain access without destroying evidence. Snapshot state, preserve hashes/logs, identify affected authority, revoke where supported, restore trusted state and verify remediation without rewriting history.

title: Developer Manual
text: ENTITY v3.4.0 is an additive Global Passport and continuous-provenance layer over ENTITY · AUTHORITY · RIGHT · EVENT · VALUE. Integrate through published surfaces rather than redesigning sovereignty semantics.

title: Architecture
text: Identity and authority remain below applications/providers. Evidence and rights bind to objects; Global Passports bind existing rights/evidence/profile state; packages configure deployment facts.

title: Repository Layout
text: Key surfaces: 01_Core_Runtime identity/runtime; 30_Universal_Transaction_Fabric objects/rights/provenance/value; 36_Adoption_Layer Rights Passports; 37_Verifiable_Reality evidence; 38_Global_Passports v3.4; 39_Implementation_Packages.

title: Identity API
text: EntityIdentityVault loads/creates manifests, signs governed bodies and verifies signatures. Applications must not treat aliases, accounts, devices or providers as substitutes for the cryptographic Entity root.

title: Universal Transaction Fabric
text: UniversalTransactionFabric registers objects, grants rights, records provenance and value, and supports governed transaction/economic surfaces. Provenance explicitly does not imply ownership.

title: Evidence API
text: EvidenceRegistry.issue_evidence binds a source Entity, evidence type, subject reference and SHA-256 commitment. Evidence remains attributable and contestable.

title: Rights Passport API
text: Rights Passports are immutable by object/version and can carry rules, custody, provenance, jurisdiction, disclosure, privacy and bounded economic terms. Legal classification remains external.

title: Global Passport API
text: GlobalPassportRegistry.issue requires controller alignment and a valid Rights Passport, resolves profile stacks, rejects normative-equivalence claims and signs the passport body.

title: Profile Registry
text: GlobalProfileRegistry stores signed versioned profiles. Stacks require a Global profile and declared parents. Conflicts fail closed or apply the most restrictive compatible policy.

title: Continuous Ingestion API
text: ContinuousProvenanceEngine hashes files, stores content-addressed custody, registers objects/evidence/rights/passports and creates a zero-value potential record. Directory ingestion returns an inventory root.

title: Implementation Packages
text: The six v3.4 packages are pre-engineered deployment assets. Configure organization, jurisdiction, authority source and package-specific policy facts, then map systems/data without redefining external standards.

title: CLI Reference
text: tools/entity_v3_4_cli.py exposes init, packages, plan, map, ingest and verify. Commands use an explicit state directory so code and sovereign state remain separable.

title: SDK Reference
text: The Global Passport SDK composes package planning, standards mapping, ingestion and passport verification for application integrations.

title: Schemas and Canonicalization
text: Protocol schemas live under protocol/. Hashes and signatures rely on deterministic canonical representations. Schema evolution must preserve interpretation of historical signed records.

title: Standards Mapping
text: Mappings state correspondence under a mapping version. They must not claim normative equivalence or make an external standard subordinate to ENTITY.

title: Create a New Profile
text: Define stable profile ID/version, kind, schema hash, parent refs, object/evidence types, policies and conflict behavior; sign through an authorized issuer Entity.

title: Adapters and Connectors
text: Connectors may provide observations/evidence and mapping, but they do not redefine identity, authority, rights, evidence/truth, provenance, economics or verification rules.

title: Testing
text: Run the complete regression suite for release-affecting changes. Add targeted positive and negative/tampered tests for new protocol- or security-sensitive behavior.

title: Conformance
text: The v3.4 sealed Global Passport campaign has 24 vectors, 12 valid and 12 invalid, with a deterministic result hash. Conformance is distinct from independent third-party validation.

title: Clean-room Implementation
text: Independent evidence requires unrelated authorship from public specification/kit material. BTG-controlled Rust, TypeScript, C#, Go, Swift and Java are controlled reproducibility baselines.

title: GitHub Evidence Bridge
text: ENTITY-GITHUB-APP is a read-only adapter that turns GitHub repository, commit, PR, CI, release and installation activity into evidence/provenance candidates without becoming authority over ENTITY.

title: Contribution Workflow
text: Issue/discussion â†’ bounded proposal â†’ implementation/evidence â†’ PR â†’ automated checks â†’ review â†’ protected merge â†’ release qualification where applicable.

title: Release Engineering
text: Releases are evidence-gated. Preserve protected commit, tag, manifest, regression/targeted results, sealed-kit hashes, CI evidence and explicit external claim boundaries.

title: Protocol Reference
text: Governing abstraction: ENTITY â†’ AUTHORITY â†’ RIGHT â†’ EVENT â†’ VALUE. The protocol separates identity, authority, evidence, rights, custody, usage and value so infrastructure cannot silently become sovereign authority.

title: Sovereignty Doctrine
text: Infrastructure possession does not become sovereign authority. Hosting, storage, routing, discovery and custody remain replaceable services.

title: ENTITY Primitive
text: The Entity root is the persistent cryptographic subject/controller identity. Human-readable aliases are resolution surfaces, not the authority root.

title: AUTHORITY Primitive
text: Authority must be explicit, scoped and revocable where supported. Applications and agents do not inherit authority merely by running on an authorized host.

title: RIGHT Primitive
text: Rights are explicit governed permissions/entitlements over an Entity object. Access, custody, registration and possession are not silently converted to ownership.

title: EVENT Primitive
text: Events record attributable state transitions, evidence and provenance. A signed event proves who signed the encoded statement, not every external-world assertion.

title: VALUE Primitive
text: Value state is evidence-governed. ENTITY can record potential, observed, accrued or realized consequences without manufacturing market price or accounting fair value.

title: Provenance
text: Derived artifacts preserve origin Entity IDs, producer/controller context, source/parent objects, evidence and rights/consent. Provenance does not itself establish ownership.

title: Reality and Evidence
text: Cryptographic verification, protocol verification and reality/evidence verification are distinct. Success in one does not silently imply the others.

title: Market Lifecycle
text: The preserved lifecycle is DCO â†’ Instrument â†’ Listing â†’ Disclosure â†’ Order/RFQ/Auction â†’ Price Discovery â†’ Trade â†’ Clearing â†’ Settlement â†’ Entitlement â†’ Usage â†’ Derived Output â†’ Economic Consequence.

title: Portability and Recovery
text: A conforming Entity survives device, host or provider replacement. Recovery restores the same authoritative identity/state semantics rather than manufacturing a replacement root.

title: Global Passport
text: One Global Passport binds an object to an existing Rights Passport, profile stack, evidence, provenance, mappings and economic state. Many profiles compose without sovereignty silos.

title: Economic Architecture
text: ENTITY does not require artificial scarcity of information bytes. Scarcity can exist in explicit rights, entitlements, capacity, duration, jurisdiction, usage quantity, derivation and participation.

title: Nonrival Data
text: The same bytes can be copied without extinguishing the original. ENTITY therefore governs rights and derived economic interests rather than pretending bytes behave like bearer shares.

title: Rights Instruments
text: A DCO/right can become an instrument under explicit disclosed terms and proceed through listing, trade, clearing, settlement, entitlement and usage.

title: Economic Participation Profile
text: Economic participation creates no protocol tax and requires no cryptocurrency. Value may come from disclosed rights-unit reserves, contractual participation and service revenue.

title: Treasury and Reserves
text: Originators can establish signed treasuries and participation policies, allocate reserves and inspect auditable positions. Allocation must follow active policy and prevent replay/double allocation.

title: Primary Participation
text: A signed policy can allocate a bounded basis-point portion of primary gross proceeds to an authorized treasury. The obligation is evidence-governed, not a protocol tax.

title: Secondary Royalties
text: A policy can define bounded secondary royalty/participation. Capture is tied to settled trade evidence and the policy effective at event time.

title: Derivative Participation
text: Derivative commercial revenue can create a signed obligation when valid policy, payer assertion and evidence exist. Policies cannot be retroactively applied.

title: Service Revenue
text: BTG or another provider may earn ordinary service revenue for APIs, certification, managed infrastructure, market data or other services. Revenue does not create protocol authority.

title: Settlement and Verification
text: Obligations may be attested by payer, treasury entity or explicitly authorized settlement verifier. External verification remains evidence/attestation, not absolute truth.

title: Valuation Boundaries
text: Ingestion defaults to POTENTIAL / 0 / UNSPECIFIED until an authorized economic event supports more. Indicative marks are explicitly not accounting fair value.

title: Security Manual
text: Protect cryptographic identity, authority transitions, canonicalization, recovery, evidence semantics, rights/settlement authorization and provider independence.

title: Signing Keys
text: Private signing/recovery keys never belong in public repositories, logs, evidence reports or support bundles. Public manifests may expose public verification material.

title: Revocation and Rotation
text: Key changes must preserve interpretation of valid historical signatures under applicable signed-time semantics. Compromise response must not rewrite history.

title: Provider Capture
text: Possession of storage, DNS, routing, discovery or hosted compute is insufficient to become ENTITY authority. Review each integration against this invariant.

title: Evidence Threats
text: Signatures can authenticate a false assertion. Review source authority, evidence type, freshness, substitution/replay risk, contestability and supersession separately.

title: Backup Security
text: Separate operational state from recovery secrets, encrypt sensitive backups, verify semantic roots after restore and retain evidence to detect rollback/tampering.

title: Security Reporting
text: Use private vulnerability reporting for exploitable findings. Public architecture critiques and non-sensitive counterexamples should remain reproducible.

title: Domain Packages
text: The six repositories are deployable profiles/packages over one ENTITY Global Passport; they are not six separate passport protocols.

title: ENTITY / CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
text: Path: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md SHA-256: 075f9820f43599dceb334f3accba68d62c32589e38ef68c750c771e48695eafc Bytes: 849 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # Code of Conduct The ENTITY project is intended to support serious engineering collaboration around identity, authority, provenance, rights, and provider-independent infrastructure. Contributors are expected to: - communicate professionally and in good faith; - critique implementations and evidence rather than attacking people; - respect privacy and security boundaries; - avoid publishing credentials, private user data, or exploit details that would create unnecessary risk; - accurately distinguish implemented, tested, qualified, experimental, and proposed functionality. Harassment, threats, discrimination, deliberate doxxing, and malicious disclosure of private security material are not acceptable. Project maintainers may moderate contributions and participation to protect contributors, users, and the integrity of the project.

text: Path: docs/architecture/ADR-0004-SOVEREIGN-AUTHORITY-DOCTRINE.md SHA-256: 33d739c1313821ed09c33fe91091bd9570db040ad78f756031d62ad5879b6f0a Bytes: 907 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # ADR-0004 — Sovereign Authority Doctrine and Provider Non-Authority Status: Accepted Baseline: SERS-ENTITY-003 v2.2, Section 172 ## Problem Infrastructure providers may possess, store, host, process, index, back up or technically access Entity-controlled information. Those technical relationships must not silently become sovereign authority, ownership, consent authority, licensing authority, governance authority or economic participation. ## Decision ENTITY SHALL model infrastructure relationships and authority relationships separately. Evidence for possession, custody, storage control or processing authority SHALL NOT establish a higher authority relationship unless an explicit governed record establishes that authority. Provider substitution SHALL preserve the sovereign Entity root and authority/economic semantics unless an explicit governed authority transition is separately recorded.

Domain Identifier `entity-domain-v1` binds `domain_id` to `entity_root`, namespace, version and status. `domain_id` is not a DNS name, IP address, device identifier, provider account or BTG account. Changing serving infrastructure MUST NOT change `entity_root` or `domain_id`. ## 2. Name Claim `entity-name-claim-v1` contains claim ID, domain ID, Entity root, normalized name, namespace, conflict state, evidence and Entity signature. Human-readable name matching NEVER replaces cryptographic Entity-root verification. DNS possession, first registration and payment do not manufacture sovereign authority. ## 3. Node Authorization `entity-node-authorization-v1` binds a node public key to domain/root, service scopes, network scopes, publication scopes, data scopes and validity window. text: Path: docs/papers/TECHNICAL_NOTE_001_THREE_VERIFICATION_BOUNDARIES.md SHA-256: 648f5519076fc4060f4591fc3090ab0148ed6854efa2b2c69357166df69a040f Bytes: 8,730 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # Technical Note 001 — Three Verification Boundaries **Status:** Informative **Applies to:** ENTITY v3.3.0 **Steward:** Blackmore Technology Group Limited **Normative effect:** None. This note explains existing public design boundaries; it does not replace protocol or requirements documents. ## Abstract ENTITY v3.3 separates three questions that are often collapsed in identity, provenance and evidence systems: 1. **Cryptographic verification** — was a specific record signed by the expected key over the expected bytes? 2. **Protocol verification** — is the signed record structurally and semantically valid under the applicable ENTITY rules? 3. **Reality/evidence verification** — what evidence supports an assertion about the external world, who supplied that evidence, under what authority, and what is the current contestable state of the claim? The separation is intentional. A successful answer at one layer must not silently imply success at another. ## 1. Why the distinction matters A signature can prove attribution to a key without proving that the signed statement is factually correct. text: Path: docs/qualification/PROTOCOL_2_MULTI_LANGUAGE_CLEANROOM_QUALIFICATION_2026-09-23.md SHA-256: 1896e604661367fe0c044144ea39cab99f57df86cc0343715624110b03e0c5ae Bytes: 8,079 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # ENTITY Protocol 2 — Five-Language Controlled Clean-Room Qualification Date: 2026-09-23 Status: **PASS — controlled multi-language clean-room reproducibility** External independent implementation status: **PENDING** ## Purpose This record seals the 2026-09-23 GitHub-hosted qualification of five separately implemented ENTITY Protocol 2 verifier/recovery programs written in Rust, TypeScript, C#, Go and Swift. The qualification asks whether the published/sealed protocol material is sufficiently deterministic for separately implemented native programs to reach the same verification result without calling or linking the BTG Python reference implementation. This is a **BTG-controlled clean-room qualification**. It is not represented as proof that an unrelated third party independently authored an implementation without BTG involvement. The freeze stabilizes wire semantics, authority boundaries, cryptographic meaning and portability behavior while independent implementations are developed. The freeze does not claim external interoperability has passed. The current full external release remains blocked until the sovereign-domain external qualification is executed. ## Governance rules 1. A published protocol version is immutable. Corrections are issued as errata or a new version; historical signed evidence is never silently reinterpreted. 2. Blackmore Technology Group may steward specifications and publish new versions, but it cannot make an already published conforming implementation depend on BTG hosting, DNS, a BTG resolver or a paid BTG service. 3. Provider possession, storage custody and transport never become sovereign authority merely because infrastructure changes. 4. Conformance is determined by public specifications, schemas, vectors and reproducible tests rather than access to private BTG code. 5. BTG extensions must be namespaced and must not change the meaning of core protocol records. 6. It is not a special protocol account and receives no compulsory fee from unrelated ENTITY activity. ## Required identities before activation 1. A verified ENTITY identity representing Blackmore Technology Group as the legal/operating originator. 2. A distinct verified ENTITY identity representing the BTG ENTITY Treasury. 3. Authority evidence permitting the BTG legal ENTITY to establish treasury and issuance policies. 4. A treasury governance-policy document whose SHA-256 is stored in the treasury record. 5. The BTG legal ENTITY and BTG Treasury ENTITY MUST be distinct identifiers. 6. Any independent settlement verifier must be explicitly authorized by the BTG treasury owner before it may mark obligations settled. The implementation deliberately contains no preselected BTG ENTITY identifier. text: Path: protocol/v3/ENTITY_DATA_ECONOMIC_SOVEREIGNTY_DOCTRINE.md SHA-256: f35894cba22f4a482d2612419c0078b132dc58e9d2d87eea8244456fcec6d7cf Bytes: 3,644 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # ENTITY Data Economic Sovereignty Doctrine Status: ENTITY v3.1.0 RELEASED / NORMATIVE DOCTRINE ## Doctrine Data may represent economically valuable productive capital. ENTITY SHALL permit data, information, observations, datasets, corpora, derived information and other informational assets to be represented as Digital Commodity Objects (DCOs). Economic value SHALL NOT require artificial scarcity of information itself. The information may remain non-rival and technically copyable while economically scarce interests are expressed separately. Scarcity MAY arise through explicitly defined, machine-verifiable rights, entitlements, capacities, durations, jurisdictions, usage quantities, derivation rights, participation rights, transferability limits and other bounded economic interests. Such interests MAY be issued, reserved, licensed, transferred, traded, cleared, settled, exercised, revoked, superseded or extinguished according to their governing terms. The originator MAY retain continuing economic participation in primary issuance, secondary exchange, derivative creation or subsequent economic use where those rights were validly established. It protects market semantics from loss of a venue database or treasury database without making raw SQLite bytes authoritative. The recoverable state includes market venues, instruments, rights balances, listings, signed orders, trades, clearing obligations, entitlements, disclosures, usage receipts, revenue rules, execution-time trade revenue bindings, RFQs, surveillance records, settlement attestations, treasuries, participation policies, reserve allocations, economic events, obligations, position snapshots and settlement-verifier authorizations. ## Logical state, not database bytes A recovery bundle serializes table columns and normalized logical rows. JSON-bearing database fields are parsed before hashing so insignificant database serialization differences do not define authority. Each table has a semantic SHA-256. Each EEP/EOPP database has a state root over its table snapshots. The bundle has a semantic root over both market domains, embedded public identity manifests, linked Core sovereign bundles and recovery policy metadata. ##

This release does not claim external unrelated-party v3 interoperability or production exchange certification. Those remain explicit post-release qualification tracks. Unrelated third-party interoperability, independent external security review, and deployment-specific regulatory/legal determinations remain external by definition.

Canonical chain: `principal Entity -> device Entity -> installation Entity -> application Entity -> governed data/evidence asset` The human-readable `.entity` alias is not authority. The canonical `ent2-...` Entity ID is authority; the alias-binding SHA provides collision-safe display/disambiguation. A principal binding is signed by the principal Entity and is revocable. A bare Entity ID MUST NOT establish user authority. An application installation receives only `INGEST_ASSET` and `RECORD_EVENT` delegation under this profile. It receives no ownership, consent, licensing, payment, settlement, capital, governance, or policy authority. For user-generated application data, the default asset controller is the bound principal. title: ENTITY / sdk/simple_sdk/README.md
text: Path: sdk/simple_sdk/README.md SHA-256: d1edb17ab904d2f8dcd5a4b19ea5385a9b5f7418bf13c14dd74e8007d2338040 Bytes: 897 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # ENTITY Simple SDK v1 This facade is the developer-facing reduction of ENTITY. It does not create a second authority layer; every operation delegates to the existing canonical identity, principal-binding, Open SDK and portability authorities. Primary developer surface: ```text create_entity create_application pair_device register_asset record_event export_entity ``` Verification/revocation helpers are `verify_pairing`, `verify_export`, and `revoke_device`. The SDK deliberately does **not** expose direct settlement, payment, verified-rights, corporate-capital or sovereign-authority mutation. Those remain canonical governed transitions. `export_entity` is a signed portable export. The facade does not yet label this a complete `Move My Entity` workflow because target-provider import plus retained controller-key continuity must be proven end to end before that UI claim is made.

Security reports should be treated as potentially high impact. ## Supported public release The current protected public source/reference release is **ENTITY v3.4.0 — Global Passport & Continuous Provenance**. Protected release commit: `2db5bff64507b8d67642122a5ff2fc73dfef9152` The separately published Windows x64 `1.0.0-rc2` binary remains a historical product build. ENTITY Protocol 1.0 remains **FROZEN_FOR_EXTERNAL_CONFORMANCE** as its separately sealed historical conformance scope. Current v3.4 qualification and claim boundaries are published in [Engineering Evidence](docs/ENGINEERING_EVIDENCE.md) and the [v3.4.0 portal](docs/v3.4/README.md). Independent external security review remains a separate **PENDING** milestone. ## Security model additions through v3.4 ENTITY v3.0.1 hardened operational signing-key creation, retirement/revocation cutoffs and recovery/rotation behavior while preserving valid historical signatures under the applicable signed-time semantics. Later releases add further security-sensitive protocol surfaces, including: - provider-neutral adoption and Rights Passport machinery; - evidence objects and typed claim states; - scoped and revocable attestation authority; - external reality

text: Path: src/01_Core_Runtime/permissions/ENTITY_RUNTIME_BINDING_REQUIREMENTS.md SHA-256: b98d120602d765376fce5d44d50cf9db012c491d399f5da1308405ef4a6ad742 Bytes: 1,101 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # Canonical Runtime Binding — core_permissions Authority: `core_permissions` Canonical owner: `01_Core_Runtime\permissions` ## Required Capability - Every authoritative operation evaluates actor, role, capability, asset, action, purpose, policy, jurisdiction/configuration, approval threshold, time and counterparty. - Authorization failures fail closed. - Capabilities are scoped, revocable and non-transitive unless explicitly delegated. - AI permissions remain separate: metadata read, content read, reasoning, disclosure, proposal and execution. - Connector or application authority SHALL NOT silently propagate to NIKI, ADAM or unrelated subsystems. ## READY Gate - Canonical authorization decisions are enforced outside `10_NIKI`. - Tests cover invalid signer, expired/revoked capability, wrong scope, wrong purpose and escalation attempts. - Replayed or duplicate requests cannot duplicate protected mutations. - NIKI proposals are non-executing until this authority and required approvals authorize execution. - READY binding pins current `01_Core_Runtime\ENTITY_REQUIREMENTS.md` SHA-256.

text: Path: src/04_Entity_Registry/rights_ontology/ENTITY_RUNTIME_BINDING_REQUIREMENTS.md SHA-256: 5160ef15bb6838d7880c0f2c3dfec5dbbdfce9e0e8390b55a9709096aef6943e Bytes: 1,031 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # Canonical Runtime Binding — rights_ontology Authority: `rights_ontology` Canonical owner: `04_Entity_Registry\rights_ontology` Source: SERS-ENTITY-002 §126 - Rights and interests SHALL be modeled as relationships, not a single owner field. - The ontology SHALL support the stakeholder/right types defined by SERS §§18–20 and versioned extension. - Verification state SHALL remain separate from dispute/lifecycle state. - Cardinality, fractional share, scope, territory, duration, legal basis, evidence, delegation, inheritance/succession and supersession SHALL be representable. - Registration time SHALL NOT automatically resolve ownership/authorship/priority disputes. - Historical records SHALL retain the ontology/schema version active when they were created. ## READY Gate - Canonical rights code validates against the ontology vocabulary and preserves backward-compatible aliases without changing old signed meaning. - Tests cover the complete required vocabulary, state separation and extension/version metadata.

Source excerpt def _collect_ids(cls,value,key_hint=None)->set[str]: found=set() if isinstance(value,dict): for k,v in value.items(): found |= cls._collect_ids(v,k) elif isinstance(value,list): for v in value: found |= cls._collect_ids(v,key_hint) elif isinstance(value,str): s=value.strip() if s[:1] in "[{": try: found |= cls._collect_ids(json.loads(s),key_hint) except Exception: pass elif cls._reference_field(key_hint) and cls._DURABLE_ID_RE.fullmatch(s): if not cls._ENTITY_ID_RE.fullmatch(s) and not s.startswith(cls._NON_TRAVERSAL_ID_PREFIXES): found.add(s) return found

Source excerpt def reconstructable_mojibake_count(text): count = 0 i = 0 while i < len(text): lead = cp1252_byte(text[i]) length = 0 if lead is not None: if 0xC2 <= lead <= 0xDF: length = 2 elif 0xE0 <= lead <= 0xEF: length = 3 elif 0xF0 <= lead <= 0xF4: length = 4 if length and i + length <= len(text): values = [cp1252_byte(ch) for ch in text[i:i + length]] if None not in values and all(0x80 <= value <= 0xBF for value in values[1:]): try: bytes(values).decode("utf-8") except UnicodeDecodeError: pass else: count += 1 i += length continue i += 1 return count

title: ENTITY-GITHUB-APP / docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
text: Path: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md SHA-256: fb63841dbbe2fad72766752f510513c22501b5a11b5ccc8d7745051a6ce0dc6e Bytes: 1,436 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # Architecture ## Placement `GitHub → ENTITY GitHub App → normalized evidence candidate → governed ENTITY ingestion adapter` The app is outside ENTITY Core. GitHub remains the source system for the observed repository event. ENTITY remains responsible for interpreting any candidate according to the applicable ENTITY release and governance rules. ## Processing path 1. GitHub sends a webhook delivery. 2. The receiver checks body size and verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` before parsing JSON. 3. The delivery is normalized into `entity.github.evidence-candidate.v1`. 4. The raw body is discarded; its SHA-256 is retained. 5. The candidate is deduplicated by GitHub delivery ID. 6. The candidate is stored in SQLite with its canonical SHA-256. 7. A hash-chained audit event records the local ingestion event. 8. A separately governed ENTITY adapter may consume the candidate. ## Stability boundary The candidate schema contains GitHub observations, integrity metadata and explicit claim boundaries. It intentionally avoids embedding ENTITY v3.3 or v3.4 internal object layouts. That allows ENTITY to evolve while the GitHub connector remains a source adapter rather than a protocol fork. ## API authentication GitHub App authentication uses RS256 JWTs signed by OpenSSL from a private key held outside the repository. Installation tokens are requested

text: Path: docs/CLAIM_BOUNDARIES.md SHA-256: efacef2c88a56647d55a7e811f36b388085c39e1ef9ef7d5764a47c21f9a2d82 Bytes: 1,294 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # Claim Boundaries Every evidence candidate generated by this app carries the following invariant boundary: - it asserts only an observation received from/configured against GitHub; - it does not establish legal ownership or intellectual-property title; - it does not establish objective truth of repository content; - it does not establish independent validation merely because a check, workflow or implementation passed; - it does not establish regulatory approval, security certification, market adoption or accounting value; - it does not modify ENTITY semantics. ## CI and security results A GitHub Actions, CodeQL, dependency or other check result is evidence of the named check at the identified repository state and time. Scope, configuration, tool limitations and operator independence remain separate questions. ## Authorship Git commit/PR authorship metadata is evidence of GitHub/Git attribution. It must not be converted automatically into legal copyright ownership, employment status, assignment, contribution percentage or economic participation. ## Releases A GitHub release/tag can identify a published engineering artifact. It does not by itself establish product authorization, customer availability, contractual support, legal rights or commercial release approval.

text: Path: docs/GITHUB_APP_REGISTRATION.md SHA-256: 06869044be2b47c976c4a521b966d5c9399abc09a2ac3dca14393f39850312cd Bytes: 1,519 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # GitHub App Registration Register a GitHub App named **ENTITY GitHub App** owned by the BTG GitHub account/organization that will operate it. ## Required repository permissions for v0.1 - Metadata: Read (GitHub supplies this baseline permission) - Contents: Read - Pull requests: Read - Checks: Read - Actions: Read - Commit statuses: Read Optional only when the deployment will ingest those assurance signals: - Security events: Read - Vulnerability alerts: Read Do not grant repository write, administration or organization permissions for v0.1. ## Webhook events Subscribe to: `push`, `pull_request`, `check_run`, `check_suite`, `workflow_run`, `release`, `repository`, and `installation`. Configure a cryptographically random webhook secret and store it outside the repository. Configure the live webhook URL only when a reachable HTTPS deployment exists. Local development can run with webhooks disabled or through an explicitly approved development tunnel. ## Credentials After registration, record the App ID and create a private key. Store the private key outside Git, outside the repository directory and outside generated ENTITY evidence. Install the app only on repositories intentionally included in the evidence boundary. ## Production gate Before enabling live webhooks, run the complete local test suite, verify permission

title: ENTITY-GITHUB-APP / README.md
text: Path: README.md SHA-256: 67b98b45f03e1924fdad6ca26037c2b00dc5020823b53d210f824e9de1bb9bc1 Bytes: 3,312 Open exact source on GitHub Preview # ENTITY GitHub App Read-only GitHub integration for turning repository activity into normalized ENTITY evidence/provenance candidates. This repository is intentionally separate from ENTITY Core. It is an adapter between GitHub and ENTITY; it does not redefine ENTITY identity, authority, rights, evidence, provenance, economic semantics, passports or verification rules. ## What it does The app receives signed GitHub webhooks, verifies their integrity, minimizes the payload into a canonical evidence candidate, stores that candidate in a local SQLite evidence ledger and maintains a hash-chained audit trail. Supported event families in v0.1: - repository and installation lifecycle; - pushes and Git refs; - pull requests; - check runs and check suites; - Actions workflow runs; - releases. The API client can also authenticate as a GitHub App, exchange an installation token and obtain a read-only repository snapshot. ## What it does not do A GitHub observation is evidence about GitHub state. It is not proof of legal ownership, objective truth, independent validation, regulatory approval, market adoption or accounting value. It never treats a passing CI check as independent assurance and it does not mutate repositories in v0.1. ## Security model The default permission set is read-only and follows least privilege. Do not publish exploit details, private keys, webhook secrets, installation tokens or sensitive repository content in a public issue. ## Credential rules GitHub App private keys, webhook secrets and installation tokens must be stored outside the repository and outside generated evidence records. The application reads credentials only when required for authentication and does not intentionally persist tokens. ## Webhook trust boundary A webhook is processed only after verification of `X-Hub-Signature-256` with the configured webhook secret. Successful signature verification establishes that the payload corresponds to the configured GitHub webhook secret; it does not establish objective truth, legal ownership or independent validation of claims contained in repository activity. ## Permissions v0.1 is designed for read-only GitHub App permissions. Any future write capability requires a separate architecture/security review and an explicit release decision; write permission must not be added merely for convenience. ## Local evidence store The SQLite ledger uses content hashes and a hash-chained audit record to detect accidental or subsequent inconsistency. Contributors are expected to: - communicate professionally and in good faith; - critique implementations and evidence rather than attacking people; - respect privacy and security boundaries; - avoid publishing credentials, private user data, or exploit details that would create unnecessary risk; - accurately distinguish implemented, tested, qualified, experimental, and proposed functionality. Harassment, threats, discrimination, deliberate doxxing, and malicious disclosure of private security material are not acceptable. Project maintainers may moderate contributions and participation to protect contributors, users, and the integrity of the project.

This repository configures the **one ENTITY Global Passport** for the Finance domain. It does not define a separate passport protocol and does not modify ENTITY core semantics. ## Release binding - Core source: `blackmore-technology-group/ENTITY` PR #41 - Source head: `2d7529fbadb4dd04840d62b751294bf9a7f70ed5` - Release snapshot: `3ff0e51ca2daabf50bc517e9c6e3438e8c150f1560cca6c99621621e3c855a90` - Package SHA-256: `768dd87fd5a29c7e2679fc2b0d4b172b8613712b148336d8fba91a3b92d0d466` ## Required deployment facts - `organization` - `jurisdiction` - `authority_source` - `settlement_policy` `deployment.example.json` is intentionally non-production until every `CONFIGURE-ME` value is replaced with organization-specific facts. ## Verify Run `python tools/verify_package.py`. The verifier checks the repository inventory and the package/source-release binding. ## Truth boundary External standards are mapped, not redefined. Package verification does not establish regulatory compliance, objective external truth, legal title or accounting fair value. Provider custody does not create ENTITY authority.

The SDK wraps existing sovereign primitives, v3.2 Rights Passports, v3.3 Evidence Objects, v3.4 profiles, continuous provenance and executable industry packages. It does **not** create authority, determine legal ownership, assert regulatory compliance, establish objective truth, or make external standards subordinate to ENTITY. Built-in profile aliases are `global`, `healthcare`, `finance`, `manufacturing`, `ai`, `robotics`, and public/unclassified `defence` / `defense`. ## Developer model The deployer configures organization-specific facts; the deployer does not redesign ENTITY semantics. ```python sdk.package_plan("healthcare", config, "clinical_dataset") sdk.map_external("healthcare", "HL7-FHIR", fhir_resource) sdk.ingest_package_file(path, controller_entity_id, "healthcare", config, "clinical_dataset") sdk.verify_passport(global_passport_id) ``` The package layer pre-engineers object types, rights defaults, evidence expectations, privacy defaults, external-standard mappings and profile composition. Current v3.3 qualification and claim boundaries are published in [Engineering Evidence](docs/ENGINEERING_EVIDENCE.md). Independent external security review remains a separate **PENDING** milestone. ## Security model additions through v3.3 ENTITY v3.0.1 hardened operational signing-key creation, retirement/revocation cutoffs and recovery/rotation behavior while preserving valid historical signatures under the applicable signed-time semantics. Contributors are expected to: - communicate professionally and in good faith; - critique implementations and evidence rather than attacking people; - respect privacy and security boundaries; - avoid publishing credentials, private user data, or exploit details that would create unnecessary risk; - accurately distinguish implemented, tested, qualified, experimental, and proposed functionality. Harassment, threats, discrimination, deliberate doxxing, and malicious disclosure of private security material are not acceptable. Project maintainers may moderate contributions and participation to protect contributors, users, and the integrity of the project.
